newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai government approves tax treaty with U.S.
newsitem.headline: Thai government approves tax treaty with U.S.

text.p: The Thai cabinet approved a tax treaty with the United States which is to be signed during an official visit by U.S. president Bill Clinton later this month, the acting Finance Minister said on Tuesday.
"The treaty will be signed later this month and is expected to take into effect from 1998," acting Finance Minister Chaiyawat Wibulsawat told reporters.
Thailand and the United States have trying to hammer out details of the tax treaty for more than a decade, Chaiyawat said.
Under the treaty, Thailand and the United States will remove the double taxation on earnings of each countries' taxpayers and exchange tax information.

The removal of double taxation between the two countries will encourage investments and technology transfer between the two countries, according to a copy of the treaty obtained by Reuters on Tuesday.
The implementation of the treaty will also make tax evasion between the two countries more difficult, the treaty said.
